title: Stability integrator weekly playbook & silo-unwind notes
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working weekly playbook for the Stability Integrator role (rotating SRE + PM pairing) to accelerate cross-functional SLO adoption and to 'unwind' silos that slow runbook stitching. Audience: SREs, Platform Eng, Product/PMs, Serving Runtime, Observability, Solutions Eng.

High-level goals (30/60/90 lens):
- 30 days: establish minimal safe SLOs for 3 pilot services, document runbook stitch points, get first canary alerts firing to teams.
- 60 days: reduce mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) for pilot services by 30% via runbook stitching + alert tuning.
- 90 days: formal handoff playbook, template exportable to other services, and SLO acceptance gating in the release checklist.

Weekly cadence (core ritual for integrator):
- Monday 09:30 (30m): Kickoff sync with service owners and oncall leads. Check current signal state (errors, latency, cache hit-rate).
- Tuesday 11:00 (60m): Runbook stitching workshop (SRE + platform + runtime). Live-edit runbook and identify external dependencies.
- Wednesday 15:00 (30m): Observability tuning: trace sampling, metric cardinality, SLO burn-down dashboards.
- Thursday 10:00 (45m): Engineering alignment: prioritization, small changes for next 48h. Confirm JIRA tickets for action items.
- Friday 16:00 (30m): Retro + handoff notes. Capture unresolved blockers and escalate if >48h.

Roles & responsibilities (practical):
- Stability Integrator (rotating): run weekly cadence, keep the response checklist current, triage cross-team blockers, own the unblocking log.
- Service Owner: accept SLO targets, commit to action items, prioritize fixes.
- Platform Eng: implement platform-level mitigations (fallbacks, canary routing, autoscale tweaks).
- Serving Runtime: provide model variant fallback and capacity tuning as requested.
- Observability: maintain dashboards, alert rules, and sampling guidance.
- Solutions/CS liaison: communicate expected customer impact and coordinate support comms.

Minimum deliverables each week (ampersand shorthand):
- updated runbook snippet (one-page) for each pilot service & link in SRE-RUNBOOK-42;
- 3 prioritized JIRA tickets (A/B/C) with owners and SLA for verification;
- dashboard snapshot (PNG) attached to the weekly thread;
- escalation log entry if progress blocked >48h.

Runbook stitching checklist (concrete steps):
1) Confirm call tree and escalation contacts (primary/backup) for service.
2) Confirm the observable: single metric to represent user impact (e.g., request-success-rate@user-facing).
3) Define signal-to-action map: what alert triggers immediate rollback vs paging vs ticket.
4) Document fallback behavior: model fallback, region fallback, read-only degraded mode.
5) Verify playbook steps on a smoke exercise (dev/oncall role-play).

Decision heuristics for SLO targets (pragmatic):
- Start conservative where customer-facing latency or correctness affects payments/transactions.
- If model-serving, prefer availability-like SLOs (percentile p95/p99) plus qualitative quality guardrail (model quality ratio > threshold).
- Use error budget policy: automated minor rollback at 20% burn in 24h, owner notification at 40% burn, org-level brief at 70%.

Escalation matrix & when to bypass: (short)
- Oncall -> Service Owner (T+15m) -> Integrator (T+30m) -> Eng Director (T+90m) if >1h unresolved for P0.
- Bypass rule: if customer data loss suspected, escalate directly to Eng Director and Security.

Inter-team unblock playbook (how we actually get help):
- Create a quick 'collab link' Slack channel using channel name pattern: #stability-<service>-<week>. Integrator creates and invites owners.
- Drop the minimal reproduction + timeline + current mitigations. Tag relevant leads (platform, runtime).
- If no response in 30m and severity >=P1, open an incident bridge and page the integrator.

Metrics to track for pilot cohort (dashboard-ingredients):
- SLO burn rate (per service, 1h/24h windows)
- MTTA/MTTR and % of incidents with runbook executed end-to-end
- Number of runbook stitching actions completed per week
- Churn in alert noise (alerts/day/service)

Risk register (triaged):
- Risk: Alert signal is noisy -> Mitigation: reduce cardinality, add dedupe rules, run a targeted sampling campaign (owner: Observability).
- Risk: Downstream partner SLA not aligned -> Mitigation: temporary circuit & evict partner if unavailable; escalate to Platform.
- Risk: Model-quality regressions not captured by metrics -> Mitigation: add quality checks in request pipeline and small synthetic tests.

Playbook snippets for common ops tasks (copyable text):
- "Trigger rollback": Confirm current rollout id, set traffic to previous stable version via platform API, validate success metric for 5m, post-confirm in incident thread.
- "Runbook smoke exercise": Run through steps in staging with 2 engineers: one follows runbook, the other injects faults. Time the end-to-end execution. Record issues.

Communication templates (quick):
- Customer-facing: "We're investigating increased errors impacting X% of requests. No customer data exposed. We'll post updates every 30 minutes."
- Internal bridge start: "Bridge started for <service> — severity P1. Integrator: <name>. Primary contact: <owner>. Initial hypothesis: <short>"

Open questions / things to decide (to land this playbook):
- How do we bake SLO checkpoint into CI/CD? (proposal: gating job that fails if a new service rollout introduces a 10% increase in burn rate in staging rollout)
- Who pays for periodic synthetic traffic in private deployments? chargeback vs centralized budget.
- Which quality metrics are mandatory for model-serving SLOs beyond latency/availability? (precision/recall proxies?)

Next steps (this week):
- Monday: runbook workshop for pilot-a (owner: Miguel, integrator: Aisha) — outcome: one-pager + JIRA list.
- Wednesday: Observability to add p99 and synthetic probe for pilot-a (owner: Rina).
- Friday retro: capture two improvements to the weekly ritual and close at least one action.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Try a 'shadow pager' for Integrator in week 2 to reduce context switch for oncall engineers.
- If Platform can expose rollback-as-a-service, document the API and privilege model.

Appendix: useful commands & links (short list):
- platform rollback CLI: rwctl rollout undo --service <svc> --to <id>
- quick dashboard snapshot (embed link): https://monitoring.redwood/dash/pilot-a
- runbook canonical file: SRE-RUNBOOK-42 (Confluence)

Document history:
- 2026-10-15 initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2026-10-22 added escalation matrix and weekly ritual details (Miguel)
- 2026-11-02 Observability tuning section expanded (Rina)

End of doc.
